cefrAlignment: Matches the B1 descriptor 'can write short, simple essays on topics of interest… giving reasons', with a supported 100-word paragraph and B1 cohesive devices.
examFidelity: The IELTS Task 2 rubric wording, the TOEFL Academic Discussion (about 10 minutes) and the TOEIC opinion-essay scoring focus (reasons and/or examples) are all accurate.
fixes: The model task and paragraph (part-time jobs for students: café skills, a second reason about money, about ten hours a week) almost duplicated the model in lesson 2 (writing-clear-paragraph). They were replaced with a new task ('Should schools teach students how to manage money?') and a new 165-word model paragraph. The walkthrough and the stated word count were rewritten to match.
The learn table example also used the part-time-job topic. It now uses a new topic (learning a musical instrument), and the warm-up question about part-time jobs was replaced.
Vocabulary: replaced 'part-time job' and 'career' (no longer used) with 'manage' and 'debt', which the new model uses.
ex3: the sentence '[Because of] the high cost of living, many families cannot buy new books every month' broke the paragraph's logic. It now reads 'these free services are more important than ever'.
ex3 gap 6: added 'Therefore' and 'So' as accepted answers.
openConcerns: Some overlap with lesson 4 on because / because of / so remains. It is short and is used here to support examples, so it was kept.
learnerOutcome: A learner can support an opinion paragraph with two reasons, each explained and backed by a specific, believable example, using reason and example language correctly.
